text: pnpm dev:host opens the dev stack (agents, loops, shell) to the network without a login
description: After de7abc26 the dev stack is loopback-only by default and refuses foreign web pages. pnpm dev:host binds backend, broker and sessions to LAN_BIND_HOST (here a Tailscale IP) on purpose; then anyone who can reach that address with a non-browser client can start agents and loops, i.e. run commands as Felix. Options: (a) trust the network (tailnet = own devices), document it, change nothing; (b) dev:host requires a login: reuse the hosted accounts and the admin gate (69a7ab7c) for the dev stack whenever BIND_HOST is set; (c) a per-machine key the phone/laptop must enter once. A key in runtime-config.json would not help: whoever reaches the UI can read it.

status.comment: Question for Felix: is everyone on your tailnet trusted to run commands as you (option a: document it, change nothing), or should pnpm dev:host require a login (b: hosted accounts + admin gate on the dev stack whenever BIND_HOST is set; c: a per-device key entered once)? I'd pick (a) as long as the tailnet holds only your own devices, and (b) as soon as a node is shared.
